title: Must and have (got) to
summary: Обязанность и вывод: чем **must** отличается от **have to** и **have got to**, недостающие формы (**had to, will have to**), **mustn't** как запрет, **must/can't + be / have + V3** для выводов.
ru:
## Must и have to: чья это необходимость?
Разница между ними — в «источнике» обязательства.
- **must** — необходимость идёт от **говорящего** или от письменного правила: личное убеждение, настоятельный совет, объявление.
> I **must** call my mother; I forgot her birthday. — Мне нужно позвонить маме (я сам так считаю).
> Passengers **must** keep their tickets. — Пассажиры обязаны сохранять билеты. (правило)
- **have to** — необходимость идёт от **внешних обстоятельств**: закон, начальник, расписание.
> I **have to** wear a uniform at work. — Я обязан носить форму на работе (такое правило).
> We **had to** cancel the trip because of the storm. — Нам пришлось отменить поездку из-за шторма.
В повседневной речи различие часто стирается, и **have to** используют вместо **must** почти везде, кроме прямых запретов и сильных советов.

## Have got to: британский разговорный вариант
**have got to** означает то же, что **have to**, но неформально и чаще — для **конкретного случая**, а не для постоянной привычки:
> I've got to leave by five. — Мне нужно уйти до пяти.
> I have to get up at six every day. (привычка; ~~I've got to get up at six every day~~ звучит менее естественно)
В США чаще **have to** и **gotta** (разг.).

## Недостающие формы
У **must** нет прошедшего времени, будущего и причастий. Заменяем на **have to**:
> Yesterday I **had to** work until midnight. — Вчера мне пришлось работать до полуночи. (~~I must work yesterday~~)
> We **will have to** postpone the trip. — Нам придётся перенести поездку.
> I've **had to** change my plans three times. — Мне уже трижды пришлось менять планы.
> You **might have to** wait. — Возможно, придётся подождать.
В косвенной речи **must** остаётся: He said I **must** hurry.

## Mustn't и don't have to: не путайте
> You **mustn't** touch that wire. — Нельзя трогать этот провод. (запрет)
> You **don't have to** come. — Приходить необязательно. (нет необходимости; подробнее в юните 19)

## Must и can't: вывод
Когда мы уверены в чём-то на основании фактов:
> She **must** be exhausted. — Она, должно быть, вымотана.
> That **must have been** a terrible experience. — Это, должно быть, был ужасный опыт.
> He **can't** be at home — his car isn't outside. — Его не может быть дома: машины нет у дома. (~~He mustn't be at home~~)

## Другие оттенки
- **You must come and see us!** — тёплое приглашение или настойчивая рекомендация: You **must** try the lemon cake!
- **Must you ...?** — раздражение: **Must** you make that noise? — Обязательно шуметь?
- В вопросах о необходимости чаще: **Do you have to / Have you got to** work on Saturdays?

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~I must to go.~~ → I **must go**. / I **have to go**.
- ~~She musted work late.~~ → She **had to** work late.
- ~~You mustn't come tomorrow~~ (в смысле «не обязательно») → You **don't have to** come tomorrow.
- ~~He mustn't be at home.~~ → He **can't be** at home.
en:
## Must and have to: whose necessity?
The difference is the 'source' of the obligation.
- **must** — the necessity comes from the **speaker** or from a written rule: personal feeling, strong advice, a notice.
> I **must** call my mother; I forgot her birthday.
> Passengers **must** keep their tickets.
- **have to** — the necessity comes from **external circumstances**: law, boss, timetable.
> I **have to** wear a uniform at work.
> We **had to** cancel the trip because of the storm.
In everyday speech the difference is often small, and **have to** is used almost everywhere except for direct prohibitions and strong advice.

## Have got to: informal British
**have got to** means the same as **have to**, but it is informal and usually refers to a **specific occasion**, not a routine:
> I've got to leave by five.
> I have to get up at six every day. (routine)
Americans say **have to** or **gotta**.

## Missing forms
**Must** has no past, future or participle. We use **have to**:
> Yesterday I **had to** work until midnight. (~~I must work yesterday~~)
> We **will have to** postpone the trip.
> I've **had to** change my plans three times.
> You **might have to** wait.
In reported speech **must** stays: He said I **must** hurry.

## Mustn't and don't have to
> You **mustn't** touch that wire. (prohibition)
> You **don't have to** come. (not necessary; see unit 19)

## Must and can't: deduction
> She **must** be exhausted.
> That **must have been** a terrible experience.
> He **can't** be at home — his car isn't outside. (~~He mustn't be at home~~)

## Other shades
- **You must come and see us!** — a warm invitation; You **must** try the lemon cake!
- **Must you ...?** — irritation: **Must** you make that noise?
- Questions: **Do you have to / Have you got to** work on Saturdays?

## Common mistakes
- ~~I must to go.~~ → I **must go**.
- ~~She musted work late.~~ → She **had to** work late.
- ~~You mustn't come tomorrow~~ (meaning 'not necessary') → You **don't have to** come tomorrow.
- ~~He mustn't be at home.~~ → He **can't be** at home.
structure:
## Формулы
| Время | Обязанность | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| настоящее | must + V / have to + V / have got to + V | I **must** go. / I **have to** go. |
| прошедшее | had to + V | I **had to** go. |
| будущее | will have to + V | I **will have to** go. |
| perfect | have had to + V | I **have had to** go. |
| после модального | might / may have to + V | We **might have to** go. |
| вывод, настоящее | must + V / be | She **must** be tired. |
| вывод, прошлое | must have + V3 | She **must have** left. |
| отрицательный вывод | can't + V / can't have + V3 | He **can't** be here. |

## Сравнение
| Форма | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| must | необходимость от говорящего / правило | You **must** see this film. |
| have to | внешняя необходимость | I **have to** work Saturdays. |
| have got to | то же, разговорно, один раз | I've **got to** go now. |
| mustn't | запрет | You **mustn't** smoke. |
| don't have to | необязательно | You **don't have to** pay. |

## Отрицание и вопрос
> **don't / doesn't / didn't have to** (нет необходимости); **mustn't** (запрет).
> **Do** you **have to** ...? / **Have** you **got to** ...? / **Must** I ...? (формально, часто с раздражением)
> Краткие ответы: Yes, I **do**. / No, I **don't**. / Yes, I **have**.

exercises.title: Must, have to, have got to
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужную форму. Допустимые варианты засчитываются.

items.text: Yesterday I {{had to}} work until midnight to meet the deadline.
We {{will have to|'ll have to}} postpone the trip if the weather doesn't improve.
I've {{had to}} change my plans three times this month.
You {{must|have to|'ve got to|have got to}} try the lemon cake — it's fantastic.
Passengers {{must|have to}} keep their tickets until the end of the journey.
Do you {{have to|need to}} work on Saturdays?
She {{must}} be exhausted after that flight.

exercises.title: Вывод, запрет, обязанность
exercises.instruction: Вставьте подходящее слово. Допустимые варианты засчитываются.

items.text: That {{must}} have been a terrible experience for them.
He {{can't|cannot}} be at home; his car isn't outside.
I'd love to stay, but I {{have got to|have to|'ve got to}} leave by five.
You {{mustn't|must not}} touch that wire; it's live.
She said that she {{must|had to}} leave early.

items.q: Last week I ___ stay at home because I was ill.
She ___ be very tired; she has been working since five.
He ___ be at home; all the lights are off.
items.why: Уверенность, что это невозможно → **can't be** (а не mustn't).

items.q: You ___ park here — it's reserved for ambulances.
By the end of the year I ___ move to another office.
Do you ___ wear a tie at your office?
I've ___ to work late every night this week.

exercises.title: Перепишите
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя слово или конструкцию в скобках.

items.prompt: It was necessary for me to cancel the meeting. (had to) → I ...
answers: I had to cancel the meeting.

items.prompt: I'm sure he is exhausted. (must) → He ...
It is forbidden to feed the animals. (mustn't) → You ...
answers: You must not feed the animals.

items.prompt: It will be necessary for us to move house. (have to) → We ...
answers: We will have to move house.

items.prompt: It isn't possible that she is the thief. (can't) → She ...
Is it necessary for you to start work so early? (have to) → Do ...
answers: Do you have to start work so early?
Do you have to start work so early

items.prompt: What do you have to do every day?
items.sample: I have to get up at six and take the children to school.

items.prompt: What did you have to do last weekend?
items.sample: I had to finish a report for work.

items.prompt: What will you have to do next month?
items.sample: I will have to renew my passport next month.

items.prompt: Recommend something to a friend (use 'You must ...').
items.sample: You must visit Istanbul; it's an amazing city.

items.prompt: Someone is late and not answering. Write what must or can't have happened.
items.sample: He must have missed the bus, or his phone must be dead.

items.prompt: What must a good manager do? Use must and have to.
items.sample: A good manager must listen to people and has to make difficult decisions.
